title: Cost, latency and the limits of an agent in production

videos.script: An agent is a loop, and every turn of the loop is a request that is paid for and waited for. This lesson measures one run of Marginalia's support agent: three requests, the tokens each one carried, and where the five seconds went. {{title}} Most of the tokens were the same text sent three times. Most of the time was the model writing its answer. {{where}} A smaller model cuts the time, and a cached prefix cuts what is paid for the repeated part, unless something at the front of the prompt changes on every request. {{levers}} Then the limits a provider enforces: an answer cut off at max tokens, a prompt too long for the window, and an overloaded provider that the SDK retries twice before giving up. {{limits}} And how to put a budget in the code, so a run stops before it costs more than it is worth. {{last}}
